claims.text: The duck broth is seasoned with a soy-sauce tare; Japanese soy sauce is almost always wheat-fermented, so the broth should be treated as containing wheat/gluten.
Broth is made from duck and water and finished with duck fat; bowls include duck loin and shellfish (clam/scallop) variants, so there is no plant-based base in the kitchen.
Noodles are wheat-based (whole-grain + refined wheat flour) and boiled in shared water; no gluten-free option exists.
All broths are animal-based (sweet-shrimp heads, chicken, seafood); shared cookware means no vegan-safe preparation.

name: 麺匠 一粒万倍 河原町店 (Menshou Ichiryu Manbai Kawaramachi-ten)

claims.text: Wheat ramen/tsukemen/mazesoba noodles (including whole-grain wheat flour) are boiled in shared water; not safe for celiac or wheat-allergic diners.
The shoyu tare flavoring the broth is wheat-based soy sauce; allergen note lists wheat in both noodles and soy sauce.
Broth is chicken-and-duck stock and toppings include chicken and pork chashu and egg; no plant-based preparation, so all items carry animal cross-contact.

name: 麺や 賀ら茂ん (Menya Garamon)

claims.text: The shop's two core bowls are shoyu-based ramen (chuka soba and sebabura shoyu). Soy-sauce tare in Japanese ramen is conventionally brewed with wheat; no wheat-free tare is mentioned by any source.
The broth is made from pork bone, chicken, kombu and seafood and the kitchen is built around animal-based ramen, so vegan diners face unavoidable contact with meat and fish stock throughout.
The menu centers on shoyu (soy-sauce-based) and shio chicken ramen; standard ramen shoyu tare is wheat-based, and no gluten-free tare is indicated.
All broths are animal-based (long-simmered chicken paitan/clear chicken soup) and bowls are topped with pork and chicken chashu, so vegan diners cannot be accommodated.
Bowls are built on house-made whole-wheat noodles plus white or black soy sauce tare; no gluten-free preparation is offered and shared cooking water makes the kitchen unsuitable for celiac diners.
The defining seasoning is white (shiro) or black (kuro) soy sauce tare, which is normally wheat-fermented.
All bowls are based on a seafood (dried-fish) dashi, so no broth is free of animal-derived ingredients.
The broth uniquely contains no pork or chicken fat — a 100% seafood dashi — which may matter to diners avoiding mammalian/poultry products specifically.

name: 麺屋 かがり 木屋町店 (Menya Kagari Kiyamachi-ten)

claims.text: The shop's soy-based (shoyu) ramen uses a standard soy tare, which in Japanese ramen virtually always contains wheat; combined with wheat noodles this bowl is not gluten-free.
Bowls are built on chicken, seafood, and tonkotsu (pork) broths and topped with seared chashu pork; the plant-based yuba topping is served in these animal broths.
The shop offers a soy-sauce (shoyu) seasoning option; Japanese soy sauce is typically brewed with wheat, so this is not gluten-free.
The bowls are built on wagyu beef fat, beef Achilles tendon, and a dashi-based broth, so the kitchen is not vegan-safe.
